title: Stored Procedures & Functions
html:
Stored procedures and user-defined functions are named programs stored inside the database — SQL plus variables, conditions, loops and error handling. Syntax is completely dialect-specific.

Stored procedureFunction (UDF)
Called withCALL p(…) / EXEC p …Inside a query: SELECT f(x)
ReturnsZero or more result sets, OUT parametersA value (scalar) or a table
Side effects (INSERT/UPDATE)YesUsually not allowed (SQL Server, MySQL) / discouraged
Transaction controlCan COMMIT/ROLLBACK (PostgreSQL 11+ procedures, MySQL, SQL Server)No

MySQL

SQL Server (T-SQL)

SQLite

SQLite has no stored procedures: it is embedded, so the host program (Python, Java, …) is the procedure language. It does let the host register functions — e.g. Python's sqlite3.Connection.create_function.

Pros and cons

Pros

Fewer network round trips for multi-step logic; logic close to the data; can be granted EXECUTE without table access; plan reuse.

Cons

Vendor lock-in; harder to version, test, debug and scale than application code; business logic split across two places.

What is the difference between a stored procedure and a function?

A function returns a value (or table) and is used inside SQL expressions; it generally must not modify data. A procedure is invoked with CALL/EXEC, can return several result sets and OUT parameters, can modify data and (in most engines) control transactions, but cannot be used inside a SELECT.
